chunks: From him, from Safwan, from al-'Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who prayed for days in another man's garment, then the owner of the garment informed him that he does not pray in it. He said: He does not repeat anything of his prayer.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.أَيَّامًا: for several days, indicating repeated prior prayers
key_terms.ثَوْبِ: garment or clothing in which the prayer was performed
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the acts of worship under discussion
key_terms.لَا يُصَلِّي فِيهِ: he does not pray in it, implying the garment had an issue preventing prayer in it
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ: he does not repeat, meaning no i'adah is required

ai.seo_question: If someone discovers after several days that he prayed in a najis garment unknowingly, must he repeat those prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who prayed in a garment and only later learned there was a problem with it related to najasah. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that the previous prayers do not need to be repeated, indicating no obligation of i'adah when the person was unaware at the time.
